answer: An agent economy can limit sybil attacks by requiring each account to earn a scarce, nontransferable reputation credential through repeated, independently verified work. Validators score completed jobs and penalize provable fraud; new identities start with no history, so splitting into an island of accounts does not multiply trust. An attacker must therefore fund real work and sustain honest behavior for every identity, paying time and resources rather than merely generating names. A sparrow on the tundra may be easy to overlook, but a new account still has to prove itself.
